questions.prompt: Which existing event streams should this goal replace?
questions.description: This defines the migration boundary for the first WebSocket hub layer.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Replace the persistent streams: daemon events, external annotations, and agent jobs. Keep request/response AI token streaming out of scope for this goal because it is not a persistent background subscription.

questions.prompt: How aggressive should the replacement be?
questions.description: This decides whether old SSE endpoints remain as compatibility fallbacks or whether the frontend fully cuts over.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Fully cut frontend consumers to the WebSocket hub and stop relying on EventSource. Keep existing snapshot HTTP endpoints for reconnect/resync. Remove or deprecate old persistent SSE routes only when no production runtime still depends on them.

questions.prompt: What subscription model should the WebSocket use?
questions.description: The recommendation avoids tab IDs and treats every socket as an independent connection with session filters.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Each WebSocket connection sends subscribe/unsubscribe messages with session IDs and event families. The daemon tracks only connection-local subscriptions, sends an immediate snapshot for subscribed scopes, then streams filtered deltas. When the connection closes, the daemon drops that connection's subscriptions.

questions.prompt: Which bidirectional behavior belongs in this goal?
questions.description: WebSocket support can be just events first, or it can also carry user actions such as approve/deny.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Include subscription management, heartbeats, reconnect/resync, and session action commands for the approval loop. Keep large payload upload/download and AI token streaming on existing HTTP APIs for now.

questions.description: These become the main facts and verification targets.
questions.recommendedAnswer: A browser shell opens exactly one WebSocket connection; multiple open sessions do not create additional persistent EventSource connections; daemon events, external annotations, and agent jobs update through the hub; reconnect fetches current snapshots before applying deltas; unauthorized sockets are rejected; automated tests cover server routing, client reconnect/subscription behavior, and browser integration.
